source.title: Stochastic resetting mitigates latent gradient bias of SGD from label noise
source.authors: Youngkyoung Bae; Yeongwoo Song; Hawoong Jeong

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures learning dynamics on noisy labels, including the fraction of incorrectly labeled training examples predicted correctly during training. It does not run the random-label or unstructured-input experiments in V1–V5.
record.gate_note: The paper's benchmark results on noisy-label test accuracy compare resetting methods; they do not measure the behaviors named in V1–V5. The figure-only trajectory in Fig. 1(b) is the only reported result that bears on V6.
record.test_reason: The study's own SGD trajectory tests V6: Section 2.2 explicitly describes Fig. 1(b) as an inverted U-shaped trajectory of ground-truth accuracy on mislabeled training examples, with initial learning followed by noise memorization. The resetting benchmarks alone would not establish this.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify a latent gradient bias associated with noisy labels and argue that stochastic resetting suppresses trajectories leading to memorization, yielding equivalent or improved generalization in their tested settings.
record.recipe_differences: Studies stochastic resetting during SGD on synthetically and naturally noisy labels; it does not reproduce the random-label fitting experiments or methods of the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Resetting outcomes vary with reset checkpoint, reset probability, batch size, noise rate, and which network section is reset.

fits_no_version.finding: Resetting improves selected-model test accuracy across multiple noisy-label benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stochastic resetting can improve generalization during training with noisy labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Noisy-label gradient contributions become increasingly dominant during training; gradient-component orthogonality depends on batch normalization and network size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise changes SGD gradient dynamics, with geometry dependent on architecture and normalization.

record.problems: The result relevant to V6 is shown only in a figure, without a textual account of its trajectory or values. The study does not directly test the claim's fully random-label setting.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results meet the row criteria for V1–V6; the noisy-label benchmark comparisons measure the effect of resetting on generalization, not the behaviors those versions specify.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowing with increasing corruption. Resetting overhead measures a different comparison.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption rates and steady test-error degradation from clean labels to completely random labels.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent fitting random labels, and whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
A separate comparison of fully random-label and true-label training, and direct identification of the shared patterns learned early.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says the text never describes Fig. 1(b)'s trajectory. Section 2.2 supplies the qualitative result needed for the V6 verdict. Resetting performance and gradient geometry do not independently establish V1–V5 or qualify V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on completely random labels or report training error and test error at chance.
Does not compare training time for true versus random labels or report convergence time as corruption increases.
Does not train on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not report perfect training fit across corruption rates or test error rising steadily toward chance.
Does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels or whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
Measures predictions on examples with noisy labels during training, but does not directly compare learning of shared real-data patterns with learning of fully random labels.

rows.subject: VCNN
rows.operation_detail: Tracks the fraction of examples with wrong labels that are correctly predicted during training with SGD.
rows.measure: Fraction of correctly predicted data with wrong labels during training
rows.note: The caption identifies the plotted measure, but the text does not describe this trajectory's values or shape as an independent result.
rows.check: The measure is accuracy against ground-truth labels on mislabeled training examples, not accuracy against their supplied corrupted labels. Replace 'figure only' with the qualitative result explicitly reported in Section 2.2: accuracy initially rises and subsequently falls as noise is memorized. Exact values remain unavailable, but the trajectory is described in the text, so cannot_determine is unwarranted. Keep the ordinary SGD trajectory distinct from the resetting intervention; the noise rate and batch size for Fig. 1(b) are not specified in its caption.

relationships.condition: Ordinary SGD on the mislabeled training examples in Fig. 1(b), using the reported VCNN/ciFAIR-10 setting.
relationships.reason: R1: Section 2.2 explicitly reports ground-truth accuracy rising and then falling as corrupted labels are memorized, supporting real-pattern learning before noise memorization.
relationships.display_finding: Ground-truth accuracy on mislabeled examples rose initially and then fell as corrupted labels were memorized.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
